claims.text: graphs.sgit.ai was built in about a month, from 21 August to 20 September 2026, to make one idea concrete: a node means nothing on its own.
claims.quote: was built in about a month, from 21 August to 20 September 2026

claims.text: A first book, Meaning Through Connectivity, was written in the first days and frozen on 23 August, its files hashed so the build fails if any changes.
claims.quote: frozen on 23 August, its files hashed so the build fails if any changes

claims.text: On 26 August the owner sent a memo asking for a brief to write three books from the repository, because he had a long flight the next day.
claims.quote: can you write a brief to write three books/pdf created from this repo and the work we have done so far

claims.text: Each book got a folder and a README as its first prompt, and three fresh Claude Code sessions wrote them in parallel the same day.
claims.quote: three fresh Claude Code sessions wrote them in parallel, the same day

claims.text: The three books come to about 100,000 words in 47 chapters, three print PDFs, every claim anchored.
claims.quote: 47 chapters, three print PDFs, every claim anchored.

claims.text: The shelf keeps v1.0.0 reserved for a book's actual final release, so a number below it says plainly that the book is still under review.
claims.quote: reserved for a book's actual final release, so a number below it says plainly that the book is still under review.

claims.text: Fractal Semantic Graphs: Meaning Through Connectivity, v0.3.0, is 15 chapters in five parts, 38,824 words and a 119-page PDF.
claims.quote: 38,824 words and a 119-page PDF

claims.text: Creating a Book Using Agentic Workflows, v0.2.0, is twelve chapters, 31,435 words and 92 pages, built from 88 tagged releases over six days.
claims.quote: 31,435 words and 92 pages, built from 88 tagged releases over six days

claims.text: The Universe volume, v0.1.0 and held, is an atlas of 90 concepts in eight regions, 168 named verbs and 165 verbatim quotes from 35 sources.
claims.quote: 90 concepts in eight regions, 168 named verbs, 165 verbatim quotes from 35 sources

claims.text: The altitude ladder shows the same book at five altitudes, each level a compression of the level below, with every highlighted phrase descending into the units it compressed.
claims.quote: where each level is a compression of the level below it, and every highlighted phrase descends into the units it compressed

claims.text: A compression puts sentences next to each other that the full text keeps forty pages apart, and two of them turned out to contradict each other.
claims.quote: a compression puts sentences next to each other that the full text keeps forty pages apart

claims.text: The book as a graph decomposed the making-of book to the word and provably put it back together: every chapter rebuilt byte-identical on the build.
claims.quote: Every chapter below rebuilt byte-identical on this build.

claims.text: In the worked example on Article 26(5) of the AI Act, five of nine questions are unanswered, and the brief calls those five the actual output of the exercise.
claims.quote: where five of nine questions are unanswered

claims.text: The team was seven roles with one folder each, and the founder's memos were kept verbatim because the founder's voice is source material and is not edited.
claims.quote: the founder's voice is source material and is not edited.

claims.text: The owner's memo after the flight said the making-of book's alignment was way stronger, by orders of magnitude, than the book about graphs.
claims.quote: way stronger, like by orders of magnitude

claims.text: The release notes give the reason: the same agent on the same day wrote book C over 41 narrated release rows, 38 verbatim briefs and a repository, and book B over an argument.
claims.quote: book C was written over 41 narrated release rows, 38 verbatim briefs and a repository it could interrogate, while book B was written over an argument

claims.text: Because every article here starts from a memo, is checked against sources and lands in a repository the next can read, books can be made from them.
claims.quote: That is why I think books can be made from them.

claims.text: After the flight the owner asked for review as change control: plan, map, define, review, approve, implement, then approve the implementation.
claims.quote: we start by planning, mapping, defining, reviewing, approving, and then implementing, and then approving the implementation

claims.text: The agents built a board of eight workstreams, 40 tasks and seven stages per change.
claims.quote: a board of eight workstreams, 40 tasks and seven stages per change

claims.text: Both change-control workstreams are blocked at the same stage on the same person, and the approved stage has two items waiting and nothing has ever passed through it.
claims.quote: has two items waiting and nothing has ever passed through it

claims.text: The last release of graphs.sgit.ai was on 20 September; the owner's energy had moved to the next place of highest leverage.
claims.quote: The last release was on 20 September.

claims.text: The owner's Leanpub books never finished for the same reason: at 60 to 70% of the content, the overhead of making changes stopped them.
claims.quote: I got to that sort of 60 70% of the content, and then the overhead of making changes.

claims.text: The workflow was well designed for quality and badly designed for momentum: every step was big, and the biggest one waited on the owner.
claims.quote: The workflow was well designed for quality and badly designed for momentum

claims.text: Much moved into this newsroom: seven roles, where we lose, readable versions, a graph per document, llms.txt and a markdown twin, and memos as source material.
claims.quote: A lot of it moved into this newsroom, which is why I do not think of the books as wasted

claims.text: The state map went the other way: graphs.sgit.ai borrowed it from this newsroom's brief.
claims.quote: graphs.sgit.ai borrowed it from this newsroom's brief

claims.text: The books are not finished: two are under review, one is held, one is frozen.
claims.quote: The books are not finished.

claims.text: The flight notes are not on the site, which records a bunch of notes but not each one.
claims.quote: The flight notes are not on the site.

claims.text: The article does not claim the workflow was wrong; it was right for quality and needed smaller steps.
claims.quote: It was right for quality; it needed smaller steps.

claims.text: The comparison between the two books is one case: two books, one agent, one day.
claims.quote: Two books, one agent, one day.
